issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Allow signed-in MapThru users to connect one Google account as an additional sign-in method from /profile → Password and Security, even when the Google email differs from the primary MapThru account email. Connecting Google must never merge accounts, move projects, or transfer billing/collaboration data.

Docs:

  • PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-11-connect-google-sso-account/prd.md
  • Brief: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-11-connect-google-sso-account/brief.md

RESULT

Branch: design/connect-google-SSO-account

Problem

Google login today is tied directly to the Google email address. Users with an existing MapThru account (email/password) risk creating a duplicate account, losing sight of their projects, or hitting a conflict if they try to sign in with Google using a different email than their MapThru account.

Solution

Add a Google sign-in method card to /profile under Password and Security:

  • Shows connection status (Connected / Not connected)
  • Shows primary MapThru email separately from the connected Google email
  • Connect Google action (OAuth) when not connected
  • Disconnect action when connected and password login is available
  • Guides the user to set a password first when disconnect would lock them out

Locked Decisions

  • Google email may differ from the MapThru account email; MapThru email stays primary.
  • One MapThru account ↔ one Google account (exclusive, both directions).
  • Conflicting Google connections are blocked, never merged.
  • Disconnect is only allowed when password login is available.

In Scope

  • Connect Google from signed-in Profile > Password and Security
  • Login with a connected Google account
  • Display connected Google status + email
  • Disconnect Google when password login available
  • Conflict / failure / lockout-prevention messaging
  • QA coverage: same-email and different-email flows

Out of Scope

  • Automatic account merge / project / billing transfer
  • Multiple Google accounts per MapThru account (or vice versa)
  • Account chooser during Google login
  • Changing the user's primary MapThru email
  • Separate Google SSO settings route (v1)

Acceptance Criteria

  • User can connect Google with the same email as their MapThru account
  • User can connect Google with a different email; MapThru email stays unchanged
  • Google login opens the previously-connected MapThru account, never a duplicate
  • Connecting a Google account already linked to/representing another MapThru account is blocked with a neutral message
  • Disconnect is only available when hasPassword is true; otherwise the user is guided to set a password
  • Connect/disconnect loading, success, blocked, and failed states are all represented in the UI without exposing raw backend errors
  • Frontend refreshes account auth-method status after OAuth return and after disconnect
  • Long MapThru/Google emails truncate gracefully on mobile and desktop
  • All controls (connect, disconnect, confirm, cancel, retry, set password) are keyboard-reachable with visible focus states

Full functional requirements (GCA-R1–R20) and QA scenarios (21 scenarios) are in the PRD linked above.

Frontend Data Contract

Field Purpose
email Primary MapThru account email
hasPassword Whether password login is available
googleConnected Whether a Google account is connected
googleEmail Connected Google email, when available
canDisconnectGoogle Whether disconnect is safe without lockout

Error categories for UI mapping: conflict, verification_failed, already_connected, unsafe_disconnect, unauthenticated, generic_failure.

  • Google sign-in card implemented on /profile → Password and Security, covering all PRD states (not connected, connecting, connected same/different email, disconnect confirmation, disconnect blocked, success/error feedback) with keyboard/focus/aria-live handling.
  • Connect/disconnect currently run against a local mock (src/lib/googleAccount/connect.ts) — the Go API has no /v1/auth/google/link or /unlink endpoint yet. Flagged for Backend.
  • getMeAction extended with googleConnected / googleEmail, read defensively (defaults to false/null until the backend adds them).
